name: ConvoTrack Dark Glass Ride UI
description: Full-app design system for ConvoTrack, matched to the reference screens (Home, Lobby, Edit Ride): photographic heroes that fade into a blue-black base, quiet glass cards, a serif headline, wide-tracked uppercase labels, mono data, and one accent accent for the next action and the route.
changelog: 2.3.2: Lobby drops the stat tiles; Ride details moves above the roster and gains a Joining code row with a copy button.
2.3.1: Implemented on Android. iconDisc is a cyan-tinted dark (#14202A) to suit the accent; appBackground starts at base to avoid a seam under hero photos.
2.3.0-draft: Hero photos supplied by the user and added to design/assets. Recent-ride thumbnails confirmed. Bottom nav stays visible in the lobby.

2.2.0-draft: Accent changed to ice cyan #3DE8FF. Bottom nav uses the app's real tabs (History · Home · Profile). Tags and statuses come from the app, not the references (no INVITED, Last seen, MEMBER, LIVE NOW or LEADER chip in the roster).

2.1.0-draft: Rebased on the four reference screens. Colours re-sampled from them; added photographic heroes, floating circular buttons over photos, the floating bottom nav with a centre action button, solid status badges, the leader row accent bar, stat tiles, the ride-details list, meta chips, avatar stacks, ride thumbnails and the glowing route line. Replaces any 2.0 rule that disagrees.

2.0.0-draft: Extended from the single Edit Ride spec to the whole app. Android (Jetpack Compose) is implemented first; iOS is ported from the result. All v1.0.0 tokens and components are kept unless noted under 'resolvedConflicts'.

platform.units: All '...Pt' values are density-independent: pt on iOS, dp on Android. Font sizes are pt on iOS and sp on Android, so they follow the system font scale.

layout_reference.device_class: modern phone, portrait first; the navigation screen also supports landscape
layout_reference.coordinate_note: Reference dimensions describe the generated concept image, not required device dimensions. Use safe-area-aware responsive layout.

safe_area.androidNote: Edge-to-edge is on. Use statusBarsPadding / navigationBarsPadding. The bottom inset is about 0dp with gesture navigation and about 48dp with three-button navigation, so never hard-code it.

androidSubstitutions.fonts: SF Pro and SF Mono cannot be bundled on Android. Use the families in tokens.typography.fontFamilies.android.
androidSubstitutions.blur: Real backdrop blur needs API 31+. On API 31+ use RenderEffect (or the Haze library). On API 26 to 30 use the opaque fallback colour each glass token names in 'fallback'.
androidSubstitutions.symbols: SF Symbols map to Material Symbols Rounded. See iconography.mapping.
androidSubstitutions.dynamicType: sp units plus the system font scale. Components with a fixed height must allow the text to shrink or wrap; see the autoShrink rules.
androidSubstitutions.reduceMotion: Read Settings.Global.ANIMATOR_DURATION_SCALE. When it is 0, swap animations for instant state changes.

design_principles: Photography first: every top-level screen opens on a photo (riding imagery or the ride's destination) that fades into the blue-black base
Chrome floats over the photo: circular glass buttons, no app bar
One serif headline per screen, set large in white; everything else is a clean sans
Wide-tracked uppercase for section labels and eyebrows; monospace for data, codes and status badges
Accent is for the next action (one filled button), live state and the route. Status colours stay solid and readable
Cards are dark, low-contrast glass with hairline borders; no heavy shadows except the accent glow on primary actions
Status is never colour alone: every state has a word

keepsAccentFill: Selected segment / selected route option chip
Small primary pills that are the main action of their card (RESUME, UPGRADE, REGROUP on the split alert, MARK AS ARRIVED, Retry in an empty state)
SAVE % badge on the best-value plan
keepsAccentStroke: Route core line and route start/destination markers
keepsAccentText: Live data that is the screen's subject: turn distance, the primary summary metric, the invite code
Trailing text actions in a SectionHeading (SEE ALL, VIEW ON MAP)
LIVE indicator and ride status on the active-ride card

demotedFromAccent.rule: Everything that is accent today only for decoration becomes text.primary, text.secondary or an accent.tint disc with an accent icon.
examples: Top-bar titles (32sp accent) become screenTitle in text.primary
The top bar's back arrow and antenna icon become IconButtons with a text.primary icon
Settings row icons become text.secondary icons
Profile stat values become text.primary (only the hero metric on Summary stays accent)
The SQUAD ROSTER label becomes a SectionHeading in text.secondary
Benefit-tile icons sit in an accent tint disc instead of being bare accent glyphs
Ready roster rows lose the solid accent border and use border.default; readiness lives in the badge
Splash and auth taglines use text.muted

iconography.style: SF Symbols on iOS; Material Symbols Rounded (outlined, weight 500, grade 0, optical size 24) on Android, giving one consistent rounded outline set

behaviors.addStop: Append a new stop input and connect it to the route timeline.
behaviors.removeStop: Remove the selected intermediate stop and recalculate route geometry, ETA, and distance.
behaviors.selectLocation: Show autocomplete results; selecting a result updates the route and metrics.
behaviors.saveRide: Validate title and route, show loading state, persist changes, then confirm success.
behaviors.routeRecalculation: Animate route geometry subtly; avoid blocking the UI while fetching route data.
behaviors.markReady: Optimistic: the button and tally update on tap and roll back if the server never acknowledges.
behaviors.regroupBroadcast: Tapping a reason sends immediately. No confirm step.
behaviors.liveValues: Speed, ETA and distance update in place without animating between values.

contrastNotes.verified: On background.base: text.primary 18.4:1, secondary 11.6:1, muted 6.3:1, accent 17.1:1, success 14.2:1, danger 10.0:1. onAccent on accent 16.0:1. Muted on the glass fallback 5.5:1.
contrastNotes.restricted: text.subtle (4.0:1) and text.disabled (3.4:1) fail AA for normal text. Use them only for separators, disabled controls, and text 18pt or larger.

accessibility.fontScaleRules: Fixed-height components (SummaryMetricCard, NavBottomBar, PlanCard price) step their text down (autoShrink) and never clip or truncate digits. Everything else grows.
accessibility.mapAlternativeSummary: Provide a text summary of start, stops, destination, distance, and estimated time.
accessibility.liveRegions: HUD banners (emergency, split, regroup, reconnecting) are announced as polite live regions; emergency is assertive.

implementationNotes: Values are design-token starting points inferred from the reference image; validate against actual device screenshots.
Use native blur/material APIs where available, with opaque fallbacks for performance and accessibility.
Do not use the reference screenshot as a flattened background; build the interface from reusable native components.
Use real map SDK rendering for route preview, including route geometry and labels.
Scale spacing and typography with Dynamic Type while preserving the visual hierarchy.
Keep high-frequency map updates and route calculations off the main UI thread where possible.

Android: expose tokens as a CompositionLocal theme (ConvoTrackTheme.colors / .type / .spacing / .radius) and map them into Material 3's ColorScheme too, so stock components (ModalBottomSheet, AlertDialog, ripple, text selection) pick them up.

Android: keep every component in ui/designsystem/, one file per family (Buttons.kt, Inputs.kt, Cards.kt, Hud.kt, Map.kt, Feedback.kt). Screens may not use raw hex, raw sp or raw RoundedCornerShape values.
Implementation order: tokens and theme, then components, then Edit Ride and Create Ride (the reference screens), then the rest of the app screen by screen, then the map style, markers and share card.

decisions.decision: Bundle Inter, Source Serif 4 and Roboto Mono in res/font (subset to Latin).
Use heroTitle / heroTitleCompact (Source Serif 4) where placed: lobby ride title, summary, membership hero, success screen, verify-email title. Re-evaluate on device.
Add a 'RIDE SUMMARY' ScreenHeader with no back button.

Destination photo per ride, cached; map snapshot when there is none.
Keep it visible in the lobby. Still hidden on the full-screen navigation map.
